text_blocks.snippet: The duration of protection provided by COVID-19 vaccines varies depending on the type of vaccine, the individual's immune system, and other factors.
According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the following is a general guideline for the duration of protection:

list.title: Primary Series of mRNA Vaccines (Pfizer or Moderna):
list.snippet: Protection against severe illness, hospitalization, and death lasts for at least 6 months after the second dose.

list.title: Booster Dose:
list.snippet: A booster dose administered 6 months after the primary series can extend protection for an additional 6-9 months.

list.title: Novavax Protein Vaccine:
list.snippet: Protection lasts for at least 6 months after the second dose.

list.title: Johnson & Johnson Janssen Vaccine:
list.snippet: Protection lasts for at least 3 months after the single dose. A booster dose is recommended 2 months after the initial dose to extend protection.

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to note that these are just estimates, and the actual duration of protection may be shorter or longer for some individuals. The CDC recommends staying up-to-date with COVID-19 vaccinations to maintain optimal protection.

Additionally, new variants of the virus may emerge that can partially evade the protection provided by existing vaccines. Therefore, it's crucial to stay informed about vaccination recommendations and follow them accordingly.
